bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in snmp_config_when OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=396102403 ``` Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: snmp_config_when netsnmp_config_process_memory_list read_premib_configs ```
bug_description.normalized: The staged libFuzzer testcase drives `netsnmp_parse_args` through long-option handling with an empty `optarg`. `handle_long_opt` copies that empty string into a 3-byte heap buffer and, because the option text contains neither `=` nor space, appends `" 1"`, creating the remembered config line `" 1"`. `netsnmp_config_remember_in_list` duplicates that 3-byte line on the heap, and `read_premib_configs` later replays it through `snmp_config_when`. Tokenizing `" 1"` yields token `"1"` at offset 1, but `snmp_config_when` unconditionally computes `line + (cptr - buf) + strlen(cptr) + 1`, which becomes `line + 3`, one byte past the terminating NUL of the duplicated 3-byte buffer. `skip_white_const` then dereferences that one-past-end pointer in its `while (*ptr != 0 && isspace(...))` condition, producing the observed AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ in `skip_white_const`/`snmp_config_when`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker data: after getopt exposes the staged empty long-option argument, `handle_long_opt` sizes a heap buffer from that tainted length and copies the empty string into mutable buffer `cp` for later config parsing.
source.value_from: The staged 226-byte `poc` is decoded by `snmp_parse_args_fuzzer` as `argc = 3`, `argv[1] = "-d-"`, and `argv[2] = ""`. With net-snmp's getopt option string containing `-:`, this lets option parsing reach long-option case `'-'` with an empty `optarg`, which is the value copied here.

root_cause.description: After tokenizing the copied line, `snmp_config_when` blindly advances one byte past the token in the original buffer without checking whether any characters remain. For the staged line `" 1"`, the computed pointer is exactly one byte past the duplicated heap string's terminating NUL.
root_cause.note: The fix adds an `end` pointer and clamps the computed `start_from` before calling `skip_white`, directly covering this missing bound check.

sink.description: Final crashing read. `skip_white_const` evaluates `*ptr` even though step 7 passed `ptr` one byte beyond the 3-byte heap string allocated by `strdup`.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 1` at this line on address `0x502000000813`, immediately past heap region `[0x502000000810,0x502000000813)` allocated in `netsnmp_config_remember_in_list`.

parser_admitted.code: while (optind < argc && (arg = getopt(argc, argv, Opts)) != EOF) {
parser_admitted.description: The staged argv layout is accepted by net-snmp's getopt loop and produces a second parsed option with `arg == '-'` and empty `optarg`, which is the sample-specific parser gate into long-option handling.

tainted_value_origin.description: This branch turns the staged empty long-option argument into the exact malformed config line `" 1"` that later triggers the one-past-end pointer calculation.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The branch is taken because the copied option text is empty, so it contains neither `=` nor a space. The resulting heap string has bytes `20 31 00` and length 2.
tainted_value_origin.note: This synthesized config line, not the original raw argv bytes alone, is the tainted value reparsed by `snmp_config_when`.

coarse_trace.summary: The 226-byte testcase is split into three fixed-size argv strings. The witness supplies `argc = 3`, `argv[1] = "-d-"`, and an empty `argv[2]`, which lets net-snmp's argument parser enter long-option handling with empty `optarg`.

Long-option parsing copies the empty option argument into heap buffer `cp`, appends `" 1"`, and passes that malformed config line to `netsnmp_config`, which remembers a duplicated 3-byte heap copy for later processing.

During premib config replay, the remembered line `" 1"` is reparsed. Tokenization yields token `"1"` at offset 1, and `snmp_config_when` computes a pointer one byte past the end of the original heap string before calling `skip_white`.
The one-past-end pointer is dereferenced in the whitespace-skip loop condition, causing the recorded 1-byte heap out-of-bounds read.

fine_trace.note: The staged file begins with byte `0x02`, so the harness sets `argc = 3`. Its three 75-byte argv slots decode to a filler `argv[0]`, `argv[1] = "-d-"`, and empty `argv[2] = ""`; only the latter two participate in the vulnerable option-parsing path.

Control reaches long-option handling. With option string `...T:-:3...`, the staged `argv[1] = "-d-"` first yields short option `d`, then the trailing `-` is parsed as option `'-'` and consumes empty `argv[2]` as `optarg`.

Source. `handle_long_opt` materializes the empty `optarg` from step 1 into heap buffer `cp`. Because `strlen(myoptarg) == 0`, the allocation is exactly 3 bytes long, leaving room only for a two-character synthesized config string plus NUL.

Because the copied option text is empty, it has neither `=` nor space, so the boolean-default branch appends `" 1"`. The vulnerability-relevant config line is now exactly `20 31 00` (`" 1"`) in the 3-byte heap buffer from step 2.
The synthesized line from step 3 is duplicated into the config memory list. This `strdup` allocates the 3-byte heap region later named by AddressSanitizer as `[0x502000000810,0x502000000813)`.
During `init_snmp -> read_premib_configs`, premib memory replay reloads the stored pointer from step 4 and reparses the same duplicated string instead of the temporary `cp` buffer.

fine_trace.code:
strlcpy(buf, line, STRINGMAX);
cptr = strtok_r(buf, SNMP_CONFIG_DELIMETERS, &st);
fine_trace.note: Tokenization works on a stack copy of step 5's string `" 1"`. `strtok_r` skips the leading space delimiter and returns token `cptr = "1"`, so `cptr - buf == 1` and `strlen(cptr) == 1` for the later pointer arithmetic.

Root cause. Reusing the token offset from step 6 against the original heap string computes `line + 1 + 1 + 1 = line + 3`. For the duplicated bytes `20 31 00`, that pointer is one byte past the terminating NUL, but the code calls `skip_white` without clamping it to the string end or treating an empty remainder as absent.
Sink. `skip_white_const` immediately dereferences the one-past-end pointer from step 7 in the loop condition, causing the recorded 1-byte heap out-of-bounds read.

allocation_context.description: ASan reports that the over-read address is immediately past the 3-byte heap string allocated here.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` in `skip_white_const` at `snmplib/read_config.c:1804`, matching fine-trace step 8 exactly.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The reproduced stack `skip_white_const -> skip_white -> snmp_config_when -> netsnmp_config_process_memory_list -> read_premib_configs -> init_snmp -> netsnmp_parse_args` matches fine-trace steps 8, 7, 5, and the surrounding replay notes in order.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The staged empty long-option argument is copied into `cp` at step 2, turned into `" 1"` at step 3, duplicated at step 4, reparsed at steps 5-7, and finally dereferenced out of bounds at step 8.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved run reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` `READ of size 1` in `skip_white_const`. The witness makes `netsnmp_parse_args` synthesize config line `" 1"`, remember a 3-byte heap duplicate of it, and later replay that line through `snmp_config_when`, which computes a one-past-end pointer and passes it to `skip_white`.

format.name: snmp_parse_args_fuzzer fixed-width argv testcase
format.contract: The exact staged 226-byte file is consumed by `snmp_parse_args_fuzzer` as one `argc` byte plus three 75-byte NUL-terminated argv slots. For this witness, `argc` must be 3, `argv[1]` must be exactly `"-d-"`, and `argv[2]` must be the empty string. That combination is sufficient to make getopt parse option `'-'` with empty `optarg`, so `handle_long_opt` synthesizes the exact config line `" 1"`; replaying that line through `snmp_config_when` yields token `"1"` with no trailing data and triggers the one-past-end read.
